subject: Optimize toolkit - pilot SOP, pricing options, and quant/batching guidance
snippet: Pilot request with questions on credits vs commit, quantization tradeoffs, and an SOP for pilot approval
messages:
From: Alexa Nguyen <alexa@fastpay.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Optimize pilot - pricing/ops questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo — FastPay's ML team is excited by the latency wins and the promise of lower unit cost if we can layer caching and quantization. Before we can get internal approval, procurement/legal asked for a clear pilot path and an estimate for expected savings. A few concrete asks:

- Can you outline the difference between a credits-based pilot vs a small-term commit? Which protects us if model mix shifts?
- What quantization options do you recommend for production pilot (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed)? Any quality/regression risks we should sign off on?
- What operational runbooks / SOPs will Redwood provide for autoscale, KV cache priming, and fallback policies during the pilot?

I've attached a short doc with their procurement checklist. If you can send a short one-pager and a proposed pilot SOW + T&Cs we can route for approval.

Best,
Alexa
Senior ML Product Manager, FastPay
Attachments: FP-Procurement-Checklist.pdf (PDF, 180 KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alexa Nguyen <alexa@fastpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-19T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize pilot - pricing/ops questions

Thanks Alexa — great questions. Quick summary up front, then details below.

Summary (one-liner): For pilots we typically recommend a credits-based pilot with a small committed credit pool + performance guardrails; use 8-bit quant + targeted 4-bit on non-critical endpoints after a quick eval; Redwood will deliver an SOP bundle (autoscale, cache priming, fallback) as part of the pilot onboarding.

Details: 
1) Credits vs short commit
- Credits pilot: lowest friction. You get a prepaid pool of token credits to spend across models/routes. Good for exploratory pilots and model-mix volatility — unused credits are refundable or can roll to a first paid month per contract terms.
- Short commit (30–90 days): gives FastPay price predictability and modest discount (~10–18% depending on volume). Better if you expect steady traffic and want guaranteed capacity.
- Recommended for FastPay: credits-based pilot with a small 1-month equivalent commit (we can structure as refundable credits that convert to commit if you exercise expansion). That gives you runway while protecting unit economics.

2) Quantization recommendations (engineering quick notes by Karthik below)
- Baseline: FP16 / BF16 gives best quality; we use it where latency is less critical.
- 8-bit (INT8/4.8) profile: good latency and ~1.8–2.5x throughput improvement with minimal quality drop on most conversational/completion workloads. Safe default for pilots.
- 4-bit (Q4 or similar): larger gains but can show hallucination or subtle distributional shifts on certain tasks (long-form summarization, legal text). We recommend running a small eval set from FastPay prompts to validate.
- Mixed strategy: start pilot with 8-bit everywhere; designate 1–2 high-sensitivity routes (payments NLU, legal summarization) for FP16/8-bit A/B and ramp 4-bit where metrics hold.

3) Operational runbook / SOP
- We’ll deliver a Pilot SOP zip that includes: autoscale thresholds, cache priming scripts, KV cache TTL recommendations, route-level fallback rules, and a rollback checklist. We’ll also provide a short runbook for on-call escalation tied to latency/availability SLOs.

I’ve CC'd Karthik for the short technical annex and Marissa to propose commercial packaging. I’ll attach a draft pilot terms PDF this afternoon.

—Markus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: FP-Optimize-Pilot-Terms-20270919.pdf (draft)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alexa Nguyen <alexa@fastpay.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize pilot - pricing/ops questions

Alexa + team — short technical annex on quant & caching tradeoffs so procurement has concrete language to review.

- Quantization
  * 8-bit (A/Q8): safe — typical latency reduction 30–50% for inference and 1.8–2.5x throughput. Minimal quality impact for classification and short generation. Recommended as pilot default.
  * 4-bit (Q4/HF-style): 2–3x throughput vs 8-bit but higher variance. Use only after a 48–72 hour A/B with FastPay prompt set. If FastPay has high-precision NLU models, keep those on 8-bit or FP16.
  * Deterministic fallback: if perplexity or task-specific metric degrades >2.5% vs baseline on validation set we automatically route to an 8-bit/FP16 variant.

- Batching + Cache
  * Continuous batching in the runtime increases tail latency slightly for sub-ms SLOs but reduces per-token cost significantly. We configure per-route max latency budgets to balance.
  * KV/prefix cache: pre-warming common user prompts (billing notices, KYC flows) can cut token generation by ~18–35% depending on repetition. We provide a small script to generate priming pushes during off-peak windows.

- Data used for the pilot eval
  * Ask FastPay to supply ~150–300 representative prompts per route, plus expected qps distribution. We’ll run a 48–72 hour A/B to characterize quality delta and cost delta.

I’ve attached a 2-page technical brief (quant-batching-rundown-ks.pdf). Happy to join a quick 30-min call to walk through the technical checklist.

—Karthik
Applied ML / Inference Optimization — Redwood Inference
Attachments: quant-batching-rundown-ks.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alexa Nguyen <alexa@fastpay.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize pilot - pricing/ops questions

Hi Alexa — circling on commercial options. Two practical structures we can offer for this pilot: 

A) Credits-first pilot (recommended)  - $25k prepaid credits, refundable on contract decline; includes onboarding, SOPs, and 1 week of dedicated runbook support. Up to 1M tokens equivalent at baseline model.
  - If you convert to a committed plan within 30 days after pilot, we apply a $7k credit toward first invoice.

B) Short-term commit (30 days)  - $18k for a 30-day commit with a 12% discount and guaranteed reserved capacity for the pilot windows. Non-refundable but converts to committed billing if you continue.

Add-ons:
- Quant validation A/B (2–3 days): $3k (includes analysis and recommended rollback thresholds)
- Extra on-call / escalation SLA during pilot: $2k/week

Operational note: for pilots with progressive 4-bit ramping we recommend the credits model; it reduces churn risk if you pause a route mid-pilot.

If that looks OK, I’ll send a one-page SOW + DocuSign tonight and we can aim to kick off next Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Commercials — Redwood Inference

Markus / Marissa / Karthik — this is helpful, thanks. Procurement prefers option A (credits-first) because legal wants a refundable/capped exposure window. Two follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm the refund window (we want clear terms for unused credits)?
2) We will provide 200 prompts for payments NLU and 200 prompts for customer messaging; can you confirm the turnaround for the 48–72 hour A/B and the exact metrics you will report back?

If you can shoot the one-page SOW + DocuSign with the refundable-credit language included, I'll nudge legal. Also please include the SOP runbook link and the quant A/B add-on as an optional line item.

Thanks — I’ll aim to have legal review by end of week.

—Alexa
